reason: No verified refutation stands: the round-1 refutations (team-game early loser who wins under 104.2c; winner choosing via the previous-chooser fallback) were fixed by narrowing to free-for-all (806.1, individuals) and removing the fallback, and the round-2 refutation (turn-order tie-break ambiguous under turn-order reversal) was fixed by dropping turn order so the winner picks among tied first losers. Derivation holds step by step: C1 and C4 pin 103.1 as naming 'the loser' as a single player, and with two losers it gives no way to pick which one chooses, a genuine gap (my tournament-document check found MTR 2.2 mirrors 103.1 for two players and says nothing about several losers, so no MTR/IPG/JAR rule or format fills it). The stipulation C5 fills the gap while staying inside 103.1's allocation: the chooser is always a player who lost (a winner under 104.2a is never among the losers, and ties are only among losers). The game cannot end with a winner and an all-tied loser set that is a draw, because 104.4a sends simultaneous loss of all remaining players to 103.1's draw sentence, which C6 quotes and leaves untouched. I accept the stipulation as the rule; the remaining open points (first loser who left the match, four-player scope) are drafting gaps shared with 103.1, not contradictions.
